correctness.rationale: Equation (2.18) evaluates the host product at delayed time, whereas equation (2.27) uses the current host product outside the history sum and reverses the kernel argument. Taking the Riemann-sum limit gives a different integral operator. For constant infection efficiency and a linear host-product history, their difference is the positive first moment of the nonnegative sporulation kernel. An exact shifted-gamma member is replayed symbolically in the bundled checker.

originality.rationale: Riemann-sum consistency of Volterra integrals is standard and is not claimed as new. The original source-specific contribution is identifying that the published rice-blast update converges to a different memory law, proving an order-one discrepancy for the paper's kernel family, and connecting the defect to the equation used for the reported calibration. The direct predecessor repeats the same formula but does not identify or repair its continuum-limit mismatch.

value.rationale: The source calibrates a biological parameter and evaluates disease-severity agreement from simulations explicitly said to use equation (2.28). An order-one memory-operator mismatch therefore affects the interpretation and reproducibility of the paper's central numerical output. The correction is mathematically simple but scientifically consequential because delayed sporulation is the mechanism being modeled.
